item.title: Lindsey Vonn keeps the birthday celebration going, slipping into a bodysuit for clothing line's new collection
item.description: Lindsey Vonn launched a new clothing collection during her 42nd birthday week, proving the Olympic champion and entrepreneur won't slow down.
item.content:encoded:
What a birthday week Lindsey Vonn is having.

Last weekend, she got the birthday festivities started out in Europe with a bikini beach day, as one does when they turn 42. On Tuesday, she was launching a new collection for her clothing line.

Hey, look, those European vacations aren’t going to pay for themselves. Plus, we know that nothing is slowing the Olympic champion, New York Times best-selling author, founder of her own foundation, entrepreneur, investor and dog mom down.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

That's all from her Instagram bio and there's no mention of being a model for her own clothing brand in there. And I guess the clothing brand would fall under the entrepreneur umbrella?

I think OutKick’s Joe Kinsey did a good job of giving Vonn her flowers in his coverage of her bikini beach day to kick off her birthday weekend. As he noted, "She could start a podcast, sit on her ass all day yapping about random topics while crushing red wine."

Destroying her leg on the slopes earlier this year would have been the perfect excuse for getting into all that. But she has more to give. Like tiny coats and white bodysuits Jake Browning's wife, Stephanie, would be proud of.

LINDSEY VONN TURNS HEADS BY HER POOL, GISELE SNUBS TOM BRADY & THE RIDICULOUS FAKE OUTRAGE OVER US OPEN FANS

This collection, which evidently can keep you warm without a top on, if that's in fact what the message is behind the second picture in the carousel, is about vibes. As if you needed me to tell you that after scrolling through all the pictures.

That's plain to see, as is the fact that Lindsey Vonn isn't your average champion, author, foundation founder, entrepreneur, investor and dog mom.

Yes, she's another year older, but I highly doubt she's taking the foot off the gas pedal and stepping into a podcast studio full-time. Not with a profound birthday message like the one she shared:

"Age is a funny thing… my perspective of life at 30 was that (especially as an athlete) I was over the hill, but now that I’m in my 40’s I feel the knowledge of life that I have amassed makes me feel somehow much younger and more confident in who I am," she wrote.

"Despite my crash and all of the things that have happened to me, the good, the bad the ugly… I’m always thankful to be in this life. Thankful for all the love and support I’ve received. 🙏🏻❤️ cheers to another one!"

item.title: Grandfather gunned down in road rage attack days after burying Air Force son; convicted murderer charged
item.description: Surveillance video captures the deadly road rage confrontation that left grandfather Nelson Batista dead on a Bridgeport street after a scuffle.
item.content:encoded:
A Connecticut man who was sentenced to 30 years in prison for a 1992 felony murder conviction has been arrested again in connection with a road rage shooting that left a grandfather dead in Bridgeport, according to city police.

Jorge "George" Ortiz, 57, was arrested after a brief foot chase Monday to end a week-long manhunt and charged with murder, criminal possession of a pistol and carrying a pistol without a permit, Bridgeport police said in a statement.

He is accused of gunning down 48-year-old Nelson Batista, a grandfather who recently laid his 25-year-old Air Force airman son to rest, in a 9 a.m. road rage incident on Oct. 12, according to a police affidavit.

PREGNANT WOMAN DRIVING HOME FROM PRENATAL VISIT SHOT DURING ALLEGED ROAD RAGE ATTACK: POLICE

Ortiz and Batista were strangers, according to Bridgeport Police Chief Roderick Porter.

"This was a random act," he told reporters at a news briefing announcing the arrest — just hours before Batista's funeral.

Surveillance video shows a man identified as Ortiz following a woman down Park Avenue as the victim turned his SUV down a side street, according to the affidavit. Ortiz allegedly slapped his hands on the side of the car, prompting the driver to stop and get out.

Ortiz allegedly punched the victim first, and they fell to the ground in a scuffle before surveillance video showed them struggling for control of a handgun, according the affidavit. The city's ShotSpotter program captured at least two gunshots, with the medical examiner later determining one struck Batista in the chest.

APPARENT ROAD RAGE DRIVER APPEARS TO THREATEN MOM ON CAMERA AS 3-YEAR-OLD CRIES IN BACK SEAT

SEND US A TIP

He died at the hospital.

Police credited tips from the community for Ortiz's capture after a woman recorded some of the incident on cellphone video and other witnesses helped identify him.

Video taken from inside a vehicle captured some of the scuffle, including the attacker getting up, striking Batista in the head with the butt of a pistol and taking off as the victim lies motionless in the street.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

A detective recognized Ortiz from prior encounters, including one in March, according to the affidavit. He had been arrested on misdemeanor drug charges in a case that is still pending. Police also received a tip from a man who also said he could identify Ortiz as the man in the photo.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Court records show Ortiz received a 30-year sentence in 1992 for felony murder. He was off parole at the time of Batista's death.

Batista's son's funeral was held on Oct. 3 in Louisiana, according to an online obituary.

Batista was an avid fan of Major League Baseball and the NFL, according to his own obituary, and especially fond of the New York Yankees. He was a father of six and grandfather of three.

item.title: Manchin calls Schumer 'crazy' for trying to oust GOP senator in crucial Senate showdown
item.description: Joe Manchin called Chuck Schumer "crazy" for trying to unseat Susan Collins as he joined the Maine senator on the campaign trail in Lewiston.
item.content:encoded:
LEWISTON, MAINE – Former Sen. Joe Manchin, a longtime Democrat turned independent, took aim at Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer on Wednesday for trying to unseat Republican Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, calling his former party leader's efforts "crazy" as he joined Collins on the campaign trail in her high-stakes re-election race.

Collins, a moderate Republican who at times has voted against President Donald Trump and her party, is fighting for her political life as she runs for a sixth six-year term representing blue-leaning Maine in the Senate. She is the only GOP senator seeking re-election in a state Trump lost in the 2024 election.

The race between Collins and Troy Jackson, a former state Senate president, is a top flip opportunity for Democrats as they try to win back the Senate majority from Republicans in the midterm elections. The latest public opinion polls indicate a margin-of-error showdown, and the latest Fox News Power Rankings rate the race as a toss-up, as do leading nonpartisan political handicappers the Cook Political Report, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball.

Manchin, who worked closely with Collins during his years in the Senate, was asked by Fox News Digital how his campaigning with his former colleague would sit with Schumer, the top Democrat in the chamber.

DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING - HERE ARE THREE FACTORS THAT COULD STOP IT

"Chuck Schumer would not be surprised of me being with my dear friend. There is no surprise there at all. I told him he was crazy in 2020 from working against her so hard and he’s crazy now to work against her," Manchin said, as he referred to unsuccessful efforts by Democrats to defeat Collins in her re-election six years ago, and their current push to oust her.

Manchin emphasized, "This is not right. She is the soul of America. She is the soul of the Senate, and he knows he needs more Susan Collins, no matter what side of the aisle they’re on. This is ridiculous."

Fox News Digital reached out to Schumer's political team and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee for a comment but did not receive a response at the time this story was published.

A former West Virginia governor who served in the Senate from 2010 to 2025, Manchin frequently broke with his party, frustrating Democratic Presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden, as well as Schumer and other Senate Democratic leaders.

As he works to oust Collins from the Senate, Jackson has repeatedly tried to anchor the senator to Trump, who has seen his approval ratings in Maine and across the country drop further underwater.

DEMS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP SENATE SEATS BUT GOP'S MASSIVE CASH ADVANTAGE AN OBSTACLE

But Manchin said that Collins is "not a Trump senator. She's not a Republican senator or a Democrat senator. She's an American senator that represents her state of Maine ... the most independent minded person I've ever met."

Collins noted that "Joe and I were part of every bipartisan initiative that passed the Senate and became law during the years that we worked together ... I just so enjoy our partnership in getting things done for Maine, for West Virginia and for America."

Manchin and Collins spoke with reporters after meeting with restaurant workers and customers at Simones' Hot Dog Stand, a famed local eatery in downtown Lewiston that's been serving customers for a century. It was the first of two campaign stops in Maine's 2nd Congressional District, a key swing district.

Collins and Jackson last week faced off on the debate stage for the fourth and final time. The senator used the debates to showcase how her Senate seniority has helped her deliver federal funding for Maine. Meanwhile, Jackson used the showdowns to position himself as an outsider who understands the struggles and frustrations of working-class voters.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Jackson won a special nominating convention in late July to claim the party's Senate nomination, which was left vacant after primary winner Graham Platner ended his campaign following allegations he raped a woman he previously dated. Platner denied the allegations but dropped out.

Jackson, who earlier this year unsuccessfully ran for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination, had campaigned alongside Platner during the primary campaign.

Collins, meanwhile, has a history of surviving Democratic efforts to unseat her.

Six years ago, she trailed Democratic challenger Sara Gideon, the Maine House speaker at the time, but Collins won re-election by nearly nine points while former President Joe Biden carried the state by a similar margin.

Fox News' Kailey Schuyler contributed to this story.

item.title: El-Sayed's past Muslim Brotherhood comments raise red flags as he eyes powerful role
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's past support for Muslim Brotherhood protesters in Egypt faces sharp criticism from Senate Republicans on the Foreign Relations Committee.
item.content:encoded:
Abdul El-Sayed’s past support for Muslim Brotherhood protesters in Egypt is raising eyebrows in Congress after a former staffer for the left-wing Michigan Senate candidate says he's angling for a seat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee if elected in November.

Two Republican panel members said there is no place on the committee for "radical views" held by El-Sayed, who has associated with controversial streamer Hasan Piker but has attempted during his bid for office to distance himself from the socialist arm of the Democratic Party.

"A man with ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, who cheered their takeover of Egypt 15 years ago, and who campaigns with people saying America deserved 9/11, should not come anywhere near the U.S. Senate — and especially not the Foreign Relations Committee," Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, who serves on the power panel, told Fox News Digital.

Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., another member of the committee, responded to the controversy on X over the weekend.

TRUMP LINKS MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD: 'HE'S A CON MAN'

"El-Sayed says he’s running on affordability, so why does he want a seat on @SenateForeign?" McCormick wrote. "I sit on that committee, and someone with El-Sayed's radical views has no business on it."

McCormick’s post came in response to a report by The Midwesterner that featured comments from Jordan Domingue, who worked as El-Sayed’s security chief during his 2018 campaign for Michigan governor.

"It is extremely difficult to comprehend how dangerous this can be if he is elected," Domingue wrote on X. "It’s especially troubling knowing that despite no foreign policy experience, he REALLY wants a seat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee."

In 2011, while working as an assistant professor at Columbia University, El-Sayed wrote an op-ed for The Huffington Post urging the Obama administration to support protesters associated with Egypt’s Muslim Brotherhood.

ABDUL EL-SAYED GROWS AGITATED WITH REPORTER AFTER BEING PRESSED ON FAMILY'S ALLEGED MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES

El-Sayed argued that supporting the protesters was in the U.S. interest and wrote that even if the Muslim Brotherhood overthrew Egypt’s government, the resulting state would not necessarily resemble Iran.

"It is in America’s interest to support Egyptian protesters’ efforts to achieve the ability to speak their mind and have a say in how they are governed," El-Sayed wrote . "If the U.S. truly wants to be the beacon of justice and liberty that it claims it does, it would behoove the Obama administration to fall decisively behind the protesters in Egypt."

In a recent town hall, however, El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrant parents, said he does disavow the Muslim Brotherhood. His campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request about his 2011 op-ed about protesters.

The Muslim Brotherhood-backed government took power in Egypt in 2012 but was ousted by the military in 2013.

'POD SAVE AMERICA' HOSTS WARN EL-SAYED TO TONE DOWN 'CONDESCENSION' ON MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD QUESTIONS

El-Sayed has throughout his campaign emphasized healthcare, lowering gas and grocery prices and addressing the cost-of-living crisis, as noted by McCormick in his post about the candidate's reported interest in the Foreign Relations Committee.

"It shouldn’t be this hard to get by in the richest, most powerful country in the world," El-Sayed said during his primary campaign against Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., and state Sen. Mallory McMorrow.

McCormick wonders why, given that context, El-Sayed would be gunning for a spot on a committee that deals solely with issues related to U.S. foreign relations.

item.title: Giants bench Jameis Winston, will start JJ McCarthy weeks after trading for him: report
item.description: J.J. McCarthy's 243-yard fourth-quarter explosion against the New Orleans Saints convinced the New York Giants to reportedly bench Jameis Winston ahead of the Houston Texans game.
item.content:encoded:
Big Blue is making a big change at quarterback.

The New York Giants are benching Jameis Winston and starting J.J. McCarthy on Sunday against the Houston Texans, according to ESPN.

Less than a month after acquiring McCarthy in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings, the Giants are turning to the 23-year-old quarterback to try to lead them to the playoffs in a weakened NFC East.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

After being used in packages in the Giants’ 27-27 tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5, McCarthy saw significant action during the fourth quarter of the Giants’ 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints and thrived.

McCarthy took over for Winston when the Giants were down 34-10 in the fourth quarter. He threw an interception on his first possession but then led a furious comeback attempt. McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards and one touchdown.

McCarthy led three scoring drives, the first ending with a Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushing touchdown and a successful two-point conversion to make it 34-18. He then threw a 24-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely, but the two-point conversion attempt failed, leaving the score at 34-24. He then led a field goal drive to cut the deficit to 34-27.

The No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft led the Giants down the field and gave them a chance to tie or win the game if coach John Harbaugh decided to go for two, but his fourth-down pass attempt from the Saints' 14-yard line sailed high.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

While the comeback fell short, McCarthy impressed and made history in the process. His 243 yards are the most passing yards in the fourth quarter by any player this season and the second most by a quarterback who did not start the game over the past 25 seasons, according to NFL Network.

The Giants went 2-1-1 with Winston at quarterback, but the 32-year-old struggled against the Saints. He threw two costly interceptions as the Giants attempted to rally against his former team.

The Giants hope the more mobile McCarthy can spark a struggling running game that has faltered with Winston at quarterback. McCarthy was the team’s leading rusher with 26 yards in Sunday's loss.

Some believed an easier debut as the starter for McCarthy would come after the Giants’ bye week, which follows the Texans game, but the Giants decided otherwise.

The Giants are 3-2-1 and sit atop the NFC East, with the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders all struggling and battling injuries, leaving New York with an opportunity to win the division.

item.title: NBA stays silent on WNBA Finals teams skipping the national anthem before Games 1 and 2
item.description: The NBA has not answered OutKick’s questions about the Dream and Valkyries’ WNBA Finals anthem absences despite a rulebook requirement to stand in line.
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries left the court for the national anthem before the first two games of the WNBA Finals, despite a provision in the league’s own rulebook calling for players to stand and line up during the performance.

Now the NBA has joined the WNBA and both teams in leaving OutKick’s questions about those absences unanswered.

DREAM, VALKYRIES SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM IN WNBA FINALS GAME 2 DESPITE RULEBOOK REQUIREMENT

OutKick contacted NBA Executive Vice President and Chief Communications Officer Mike Bass on Tuesday.

The inquiry asked about the NBA’s role in the matter, possible discipline and whether the teams would be instructed to be present for the anthem before Wednesday’s Game 3.

The NBA did not respond by the deadline. The WNBA and both teams also have not answered OutKick’s repeated inquiries.

The WNBA’s 2026 official rulebook calls for players, coaches and trainers to stand and line up along the sidelines or foul line during the national anthem.

OutKick asked Bass whether the NBA has a role in overseeing or enforcing that provision, or whether enforcement is solely the WNBA’s responsibility.

We also asked whether NBA Commissioner Adam Silver or anyone at the NBA league office had discussed the absences with WNBA leadership and, if so, what guidance had been provided.

WNBA SILENT AS FINALS TEAMS SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM DESPITE RULE REQUIRING PLAYERS TO STAND IN LINE

Additional questions covered whether either team had received an exemption, whether discipline was planned or under consideration, and whether the teams would be instructed to be on the court for Game 3.

The NBA was given until the end of Tuesday to respond.

Bass’s responsibilities span both leagues. His 2026 Sports PR Summit biography says he oversees public relations, including basketball and business communications, for the NBA and WNBA, among other leagues.

The NBA’s involvement in the WNBA dates to its creation: the NBA Board of Governors approved the women’s league in 1996.

In February 2021, Bass issued an official NBA statement reiterating the league’s requirement that teams play the national anthem.

The statement said "all teams will play the national anthem in keeping with longstanding league policy."

That statement addressed playing the anthem. OutKick’s current questions concern whether WNBA teams must be on the court during the performance.

Before Saturday’s WNBA Finals opener and Monday’s Game 2, both teams left the floor ahead of the anthem and returned within seconds of the performance ending.

OutKick contacted the WNBA, Dream and Valkyries after Game 1 and followed up with all three Sunday, asking about the absences, the league’s anthem requirements and plans for Game 2.

After both teams were absent again Monday, OutKick followed up with all three Tuesday, seeking explanations and asking about plans for Game 3.

OutKick attended five pregame and postgame press conferences Saturday, plus both coaches’ pregame and postgame press conferences Monday. OutKick was not called on to ask a question at any of the nine sessions.

The WNBA has a written provision calling for players to be on the floor for the anthem, but its Finals teams have twice been absent.

Asked about it, the NBA has been just as quiet as the WNBA.

item.title: Newsom spars with Trump-appointed prosecutor over 20,000 suspected noncitizens on voter rolls
item.description: Gavin Newsom and Bill Essayli clashed over noncitizen voting after an LA County official said the registrar cannot verify voter citizenship.
item.content:encoded:
Governor Gavin Newsom and Bill Essayli, a Trump-appointed federal prosecutor in California, sparred on social media this week about whether the state is doing enough to prevent noncitizens from voting.

Essayli, the first assistant U.S. attorney for California's Central District, surfaced a court document filed Tuesday in which a Los Angeles County election official said the registrar's office "is not equipped or authorized to verify voter citizenship because it does not independently house citizenship-related information beyond the voter attestation."

The official, Monica Flores, made the declaration as part of a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to force California to verify the citizenship of more than 20,000 people the federal government believes are likely noncitizens who were sent mail ballots ahead of this year's midterm elections.

Essayli called Flores' statement a "massive concession" that shows election officials take voters' word on whether they are a citizen.

STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS

"American citizens’ votes are being diluted in California," Essayli wrote.

In response, Newsom's press office account on X said California adheres to a 1993 federal law that requires people registering to vote through the DMV to swear under penalty of perjury that they are eligible, including that they are U.S. citizens. Similar attestation requirements apply to federal mail-in voter registration forms.

"May want to brush up on your election law before tweeting," Newsom's office wrote in a jab at Essayli. "Perhaps Second Assistant is more apt from now on?"

Essayli fired back by citing two federal statutes that make it unlawful for noncitizens to vote in federal elections.

‘RAW MATERIAL FOR ELECTION FRAUD’: EXPERT FLAGS VOTER-ROLL PROBLEMS FAR BEYOND ONE STATE

The public spat highlighted the central dispute in the lawsuit against California: whether the state should take additional steps to verify the citizenship of voters when the federal government flags potential issues with the rolls.

According to the Justice Department's complaint, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) cross-checked California voter registration records with federal immigration data.

That investigative process, described by DOJ lawyers as "preliminary," yielded a list of more than 20,000 registered voters federal investigators identified as likely noncitizens. California voters were mailed ballots beginning Oct. 1.

In its initial complaint filed Oct. 15, the Justice Department asked a federal court to require California to set aside mail ballots associated with people on the list until their citizenship could be verified.

Flores, an official with the LA County Registrar's Office, argued that doing so is now virtually impossible because once a ballot's signature is verified, it is removed from its identifying envelope and processed alongside hundreds of thousands of others.

DOJ OFFICIAL DEFENDS TRUMP'S NONCITIZEN VOTER PROBE ON '60 MINUTES,' ACCUSES SHOW OF EDITING OUT HER ANSWERS

As of Tuesday, the county has processed 331,000 ballots, according to Flores' statement in court.

She also pointed out that the registrar's office is "not an investigative agency," adding that she was unaware of "any state or federal law granting it investigative authority."

Nonetheless, staff from the registrar's office reviewed a sample of 200 records from the Justice Department list that had LA County addresses.

"The October list is unreliable: 112 of the 200 records correspond to registrations that are canceled or inactive," according to Flores' statement. "Of the voters where birthplace was meaningfully reported, 38.9% indicate that they were born in the United States, which is strong evidence of citizenship; and 71.2% of the records have no voting history."

In a statement to Fox News, Essayli said these reported numbers "are meaningless because, by their own admission, they have no way to verify anyone's citizenship status or their birthplace."

There are indications that the Justice Department list does contain at least some individuals who could have broken the law.

On Monday, the Justice Department charged 28 individuals off that list, all lawful permanent residents, with making false statements on naturalization applications and fraudulently registering to vote. Most of them cast unlawful ballots in elections, officials said.

item.title: Randy Houser opens up about his lifelong love of fishing and unforgettable trip with Navy SEALs
item.description: From fishing in Mississippi to unforgettable days on the water with Navy SEALs, Randy Houser shares why the outdoors will always be part of his life.
item.content:encoded:
Country music star Randy Houser spends a lot of his life on the road, but when the shows are over and the tour bus stops rolling, there's usually one thing on his mind.

Finding somewhere to fish.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

"When I get off the tour bus, I'm literally looking for some water to get on," Houser told OutKick OutDoors in an exclusive interview.

For the Mississippi native, that love of fishing started long before the hit songs, sold-out shows and life on the road.

"Growing up in Mississippi, that's about all we had. We had bluegill, catfish and bass," he said.

These days, Houser's fishing adventures have taken him a little farther from home. He's traded the freshwater lakes of Mississippi for the turquoise waters of the Bahamas, where he's developed a particular fondness for fly fishing.

"I spend a lot of time bonefishing in the Bahamas. That's kind of my thing now, as I enjoy fly fishing for bonefish and permit and things like that," he explained. "I spend a lot of my time doing that in the winter."

And while getting away from the demands of touring is certainly part of the appeal, Houser's connection to the water runs deeper than simply needing a vacation.

"I think that stems from all the time I spent on the water as a kid," he said.

It's also a passion he shares with his wife and children, who frequently join him on the water.

But one of Houser's most memorable fishing experiences wasn't about the size of the fish or the destination. It was about the people he shared it with.

The country star recalled a three-day bonefishing trip to Blackfly Lodge in the Bahamas with the Navy SEAL Foundation, where he spent time alongside active and retired Navy SEALs.

"I'm a huge supporter of our military and military families and personnel," Houser said. "To get that time with those guys and get them in a space where they're on the water and can relax, and just to hear stories that they wouldn't normally talk about in a different situation, was just priceless."

For Houser, the opportunity to connect with those men away from their everyday responsibilities made the trip unforgettable.

"I got to hear just personal experiences from those guys," he said. "I'll remember it forever. It was really cool."

Now, Houser is preparing to bring his love of music and fishing together in a big way.

On Friday, Oct. 30, he'll perform alongside his friend and fellow country star Riley Green at The Pinnacle in Nashville as part of The Champions, a new professional bass fishing tournament hosted by World Bass Enterprises.

The tournament, held on Old Hickory Lake, brings together top anglers from the Bassmaster Elite Series and Major League Fishing's Bass Pro Tour to compete for a record $3.25 million purse, including $1.25 million for the winner.

For someone who grew up fishing for fun in Mississippi, Houser said it's remarkable to see just how far competitive bass fishing has come.

He recalled learning that a friend's son was competing on a college bass fishing team and thinking about how different things were when he was growing up.

"I thought, wow, what a dream," he said. "If I was in high school, I'd have been thinking, 'Lord, you mean I can get a scholarship to go fishing?'"

SUPERMOTOCROSS CHAMPION LEVI KITCHEN WANTS TO TRY TOURNAMENT BASS FISHING WHEN HE HANGS UP HIS HELMET

Houser compared the difficulty of becoming a successful professional angler to making it as a professional golfer, noting the tremendous skill, sponsorships and resources necessary to compete at the highest level.

And he believes Nashville is the perfect place to showcase how much the sport has grown.

"There's a strong synergy between country music, country music listeners and bass fishing," he said.

With Old Hickory and Percy Priest lakes nearby, Houser is familiar with the area's fishing opportunities. He's spent plenty of time fishing Old Hickory himself and expects The Champions to draw a significant crowd, both for the concerts and the competition.

"I think they're going to have a lot more fans than they expected," he said. "Not just for the music at The Pinnacle, but also hanging out at the lake waiting for the weigh-ins and things like that."

Houser is especially looking forward to performing with Green, whom he considers a good friend. The two have spent plenty of time touring together, although their busy schedules haven't allowed for much fishing lately.

They do, however, have plans to do some hunting together once the weather cools down.

Another bonus of The Champions taking place in Nashville? Houser gets to bring his children to the show — something he said doesn't happen very often.

For a man who grew up with a fishing rod in his hands, it's a fitting opportunity to celebrate just how far the sport has come while sharing the experience with his own family.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

And once the concert is over and Houser climbs back aboard that tour bus, there's a pretty good chance he'll already be thinking about his next trip to the water.

item.title: Greta Thunberg joins Paris protests, underscoring radical three-way alliance
item.description: Greta Thunberg urged followers to mobilize for Paris protests days before demonstrations turned violent, joining a vast network of 54 organizations.
item.content:encoded:
Climate activist Greta Thunberg has joined French agitators, lending her "How dare you?" indignation to demonstrations that began over education grievances but soon devolved into violent, migrant-driven riots.

In a video posted to her Instagram, Thunberg encouraged agitators to attend what became a clash between rioters, law enforcement and local business owners – calling on her followers to support the cause.

"French students are out continuously facing extreme police brutality just for asking for their basic rights. And now it’s time for us to step up because they cannot carry this alone," Thunberg said. "They are showing the world, leading by example, what it looks like when young people are stepping up when the system at large is neglecting them systematically."

GRETA THUNBERG JOINS MASSIVE FRENCH STUDENT PROTESTS AS CARS BURN, POLICE FIRE TEAR GAS

"We are asking all of you to contribute with what you can, support them out on the streets, donate and come to the mobilization on Oct. 17," she added.

The video was highlighted by the Al Jazeera Media Network on X, which noted Thunberg’s use of the phrase "bismillah, c’est les ténèbres," which translates to "In the name of God, it’s darkness." The phrase has become a slogan for protesters in France.

TEEN'S HAND BLOWN OFF BY POLICE GRENADE DURING FRENCH STUDENT PROTESTS: REPORT

While Thunberg is most notably known for her climate advocacy, describing herself as an "autistic & bipolar climate justice activist," she has been vocal on the conflict between Israel and Gaza. Last year, the 23-year-old activist attempted to reach Gaza by joining the Global Sumud Flotilla, demanding a humanitarian corridor before being intercepted and detained by Israeli authorities.

Days after Thunberg’s social media post calling for mobilization in Paris, she collaborated with the Palestinian Youth Movement in a separate post that defined "the genocidal Israeli army" as "the killers of children."

Watchdogs have noted a rise in the "red-green-green alliance," an ideological overlap between three elements: communist movements, characterized by the color red; Islamist activism, described as green; and environmental protest groups, also symbolized as green.

The result is that the same loose group of activists and organizations support a wide array of seemingly unconnected causes. In June 2024, protesters gathered outside Citibank headquarters in New York City under the banner that "Climate Justice Means Free Palestine."

GLOBAL 'CHAOS INC' GROWS TO 101 GROUPS WITH PLANS FOR NEW ROUNDS OF DEMONSTRATIONS

As Thunberg, who became an international darling of the Left in 2019, when she lectured grownups at the UN Climate Action Summit, called on her followers to join the French protests, a network of global communist parties and revolutionary groups also prepared to take to the streets. With Palestinian flags flying alongside student-backed organizations in Paris, the "red-green-green" came into light.

item.title: Best hiking spots to try in the DFW area ahead of SMU's week eight home showdown with Cal
item.description: Cedar Ridge Preserve, Arbor Hills, and more hidden hiking trails near SMU Mustangs' campus make DFW a surprising fall destination for outdoors lovers.
item.content:encoded:
As we ascend deeper and deeper into the college football season, the hiking becomes more and more about finding places that aren't frigid.

If you're looking for a locale that offers comfortable fall temperatures without having to pack a parka, might I suggest the Dallas-Ft. Worth area?

It just so happens the 23rd-ranked SMU Mustangs are hosting the Cal Golden Bears this Saturday, and their stadium, located in the scenic Highland Park neighborhood of Dallas, is within driving distance of a ton of great trails.

FSU-SMU GAME TURNS INTO OLD-SCHOOL FOOTBALL AFTER STADIUM POWER OUTAGE WIPES OUT IN-GAME COMMUNICATION

Most people likely think of DFW as nothing but a vast sea of highways and high rises, but having been a resident of the Metroplex for six years, I can attest that there are plenty of beautiful hikes just waiting to be found.

Get to know some of these hidden gems as you make your way to North Texas for the game this weekend.

BEST HIKES TO TRY AROUND LUBBOCK AHEAD OF TEXAS TECH'S WEEK ONE MATCHUP WITH ABILENE CHRISTIAN

As I mentioned, you might think DFW is just some sprawling urban nightmare with nothing but flat terrain, but our top choice on this list debunks that misconception right from the jump.

Cedar Ridge Preserve is located roughly 15 miles southwest of downtown Dallas and features nearly nine miles of hilly trails and scenic overlooks thanks to being nearly 800 feet above sea level.

The wooded hiking trails will make you feel like you are hundreds of miles away from civilization despite being just a stone's throw from one of the most populous cities in America; the best of both worlds!

If you want a taste of Texas Hill Country without ever having to leave the DFW Metroplex, put Cedar Ridge Preserve on your list.

I might be a little biased on this one since it's where I had one of my first dates with my now-wife and was the site of our engagement photos, but Arbor Hills Nature Preserve is a must-see for anyone visiting Dallas during the fall.

Located in the nearby suburb of Plano, Arbor Hills is a straight shot up the Dallas North Tollway and is a bit more central in terms of location than Cedar Ridge, but this place really has it all.

Both paved and unpaved trails are offered here as well as a bike path for anyone looking to explore on two wheels.

A special mention has to be made to the observation tower at the center of the park, which features a great view of the fall foliage of North Texas.

Make your way to the top of the tower at sunset and the scenes from up there will surely be Instagram-worthy.

Arbor Hills has wooded paths, open prairies, and even a creek, presenting the whole package to any outdoorsman without ever leaving the confines of the city.

Don't forget, there is an "FW" in the "DFW" area, and Fort Worth might be an even better hiking city than its more famous sister.

For those of you interested in a more western flavor to your trip, Fort Worth is the place to be, and the Fort Worth Nature Center and Refuge is the gold standard of Tarrant County trails.

NATIONAL PARK SERVICE DIRECTOR CALLS YELLOWSTONE'S WILD BISON RECOVERY AN 'INCREDIBLE CONSERVATION STORY'

The Refuge is super distinctive in its looks, with tree-covered trails and wetlands that connect to both the Trinity River and Lake Worth.

This place has everything from a boardwalks to natural paths and there are even bison on the property.

It's a bit of a trek from SMU's campus, but if you're in DFW for the whole weekend, I would recommend giving it a look and then enjoying some of the excellent barbecue in the area to refuel.

The final entry on our list is a bit of a local hidden gem, but it shouldn't be too hard to find.

Nestled just to the southwest of downtown Dallas, Oak Cliff Nature Preserve is a 121-acre sanctuary with thick, overgrown vegetation and dirt paths to remind you that there is still plenty of natural beauty in this overgrown concrete jungle.

There is one interconnected single track that takes you around the property, but it stretches nearly eight miles, so those of you looking to hit your step goal will be in heaven.

Bikers are welcome, too, as the nature preserve is very popular with mountain bike enthusiasts.

Anyone looking for a no-frills alternative to walking around the downtown area should definitely give this place a hard look, and history buffs will be happy, as the Oak Cliff Nature Preserve is just a short drive from the Texas Theater, where alleged JFK assassin Lee Harvey Oswald snuck into a movie while on the run from Dallas police.

item.title: Fishing trip turns into nightmare as California man, 12-year-old boy disappear in storm
item.description: A man and his 12-year-old nephew vanished during a fishing trip in the Sea of Cortez as Tropical Storm Rachel brought dangerous weather. Crews have been searching for them.
item.content:encoded:
A family is hoping for answers after a California man and his 12-year-old nephew disappeared during a fishing trip off Mexico.

Oscar Ulloa and his nephew were reported missing in the Sea of Cortez near San Felipe, Baja California, according to a Facebook post from Ulloa's cousin, Alistair Barradell.

"My family is going through a very difficult time right now," Barradell wrote. "My cousin Oscar is missing at sea in the Sea of Cortez near San Felipe, Baja California, along with his 12-year-old nephew."

DOZENS MISSING AFTER PASSENGER FERRY SINKS AS RESCUERS SCOUR SOUTH PACIFIC COASTLINE

The pair had gone out for a fishing trip on Saturday, Oct. 10 — and have not been heard from since, according to reports.

Their disappearance came as Tropical Storm Rachel brought dangerous weather to the region.

Barradell said the family is hoping for their safe return and is asking people who have been fishing or traveling in the area to share any information that could help.

"You never know who might see it or who might have information that could help," he wrote.

A search has been underway by air and sea, with Mexican authorities working to locate the missing boat.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Barradell told NBC San Diego that the Mexican coast guard was conducting aerial searches and that the family had also hired a private plane to help. 

He said the family does not know whether the boat experienced engine trouble or something more serious as the weather worsened.

"During that time, the weather did turn bad, so we're not sure if we had engine problems or something more catastrophic," Barradell told the outlet.

Mexican naval authorities have deployed six units and a specialized search aircraft, with crews searching more than 9,900 square nautical miles, according to reports.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Crews reportedly spotted a cooler and life jacket during the search, though authorities have not confirmed whether either item was connected to the missing boat.

As efforts continue, Barradell is asking people around the Sea of Cortez to remain on the lookout.

"Any information could make a difference," he wrote. "Please keep Oscar and the young boy in your thoughts and prayers."

"Please share, share, share. Help us bring them home."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre Mexico for comment.

item.title: David Spade tells critics to ‘relax’ as Shane Gillis faces backlash over ‘SNL’ joke
item.description: David Spade and Dana Carvey defend Shane Gillis after his "Saturday Night Live" monologue joke about women at the gym sparked widespread backlash.
item.content:encoded:
David Spade thinks people have gotten a little too comfortable being offended.

Spade defended comedians' right to push boundaries, even when their material doesn't land during an episode of his podcast, "Fly on the Wall with Dana Carvey and David Spade."

Comedian Shane Gillis sparked backlash after he mocked women at the gym during his "Saturday Night Live" monologue.

"I haven’t been to the gym in so long. I didn’t know women just dress like whores now?" Gillis said. "Look, I'm sorry, there's no other way to describe … Have you seen the shorts? Those neon, they're like, artificial bait-colored [shorts], and the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole. And don’t look! You’re not allowed to look."

JOE ROGAN DEFENDS SHANE GILLIS FROM 'WORD POLICE' AFTER SNL JOKE SPARKS LIBERAL UPROAR

Carvey wasn't buying the outrage surrounding Gillis' joke. Rather than viewing the remarks as an attack on women, the comedian argued that the backlash overlooked a fundamental part of stand-up comedy: saying things that aren't meant to be taken literally.

"I just didn't understand the kerfuffle," Carvey said. "Only 'cause to me, I just saw it as what we call – I'll just say it – a joke. Like he didn't – when you say jokes, you're not literally saying women are whores. You are literally joking. Isn't that kind of the idea? No? Did I just get canceled?"

Spade's assistant and executive producer of the podcast, Heather Santoro, chimed in with a different take, arguing that offensive humor still needs to deliver laughs.

"The joke has to be actually funny," Santoro could be heard saying off mic. "If you're gonna like call a woman a whore, it's gotta be funny. And it wasn't."

Carvey argued that in comedy clubs, he'd bet the joke "destroyed," but "Saturday Night Live" simply was "not the right place" for it.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"He got some laughs, but, of course, I think he knows that one's gonna be a button pusher," Spade noted. "But he doesn't care."

"Young, very highly dressed-up young women is the majority of the audience at 'SNL,'" Carvey conceded. "So, All right, Heather, I agree with you."

Spade also called out what he viewed as Hollywood's double standards, questioning why some people face criticism while others are seemingly off-limits – and suggesting that not every joke or celebrity controversy needs to spark outrage.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I will say it's almost comical that there's people that say, 'Oh, don't make fun of OnlyFans. Don't make fun of strippers. These are sex workers. They need to be respected.' And then everyone hates Sydney Sweeney," Spade said. "And it's like, 'Which one is it?' Like, you know what I mean? Let's all decide what we hate and don't and how about we just relax."

"Sometimes people just need to mind their biz," Spade said. "Like, we don't need to comment on everything."

"We do," he joked, speaking about himself and Carvey, "because everyone loves that we do."

Carvey suggested that audiences have increasingly blurred the line between finding a joke unfunny and believing it shouldn't be told at all.

"It's the idea of like – there's two things. Joke is funny – eh. Joke is not funny, joke offends me – joke should not be allowed to be said," Carvey explained.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Spade, who appeared on "SNL" from 1990 until 1996, explained that the show's comedians often face a different level of scrutiny when a controversial joke falls flat.

"I think at ‘SNL,’ If something kills, it gets a pass. If something totally bombs, then they get a lot of trouble," he noted.

"Well, did it kill it at dress [rehearsal]?" Carver questioned.

"Oh, I don't know. I don't think Shane has talked about it," Spade added. "I think he's that kind of Chappelle where he just does it, and he walks away and then everyone fights over it."

item.title: Larry David mocks socialists in satirical essay, drawing criticism over Israel jokes
item.description: Larry David's satirical DSA essay imagined relocating Israelis to a Pacific island and sending offensive comedians to sensitivity training facilities.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Larry David drew criticism from democratic socialists after writing a satirical essay mocking the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), its anti-Israel positions and political correctness, while a California political activist mocked those who took offense at the "Curb Your Enthusiasm" creator's humor.

David's October 17 essay in Air Mail, titled "The View from Here," imagined the longtime Hollywood liberal joining the DSA and successfully proposing 12 increasingly over-the-top additions to the socialist organization's manifesto. His targets included immigration, policing, reparations, religious identity and restrictions on offensive comedy.

Among the most provocative proposals was David's imagined solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, which involved transferring all of Israel's territory to Palestinians and relocating Israelis to a remote Pacific island.

QUIET PART OUT LOUD: ANTI-ISRAEL MOBS WANT ONE STATE CALLED 'PALESTINE,' ERASING ISRAEL

"We strongly believe in a two-state solution," he said. "To this end, we propose that Palestinians should be given all the land currently occupied by Israel and that Israel should be given Pitcairn Island in the South Pacific, where the weather is beautiful and grapefruits are aplenty. We think the Bagel People will be very happy there."

Lisa Cusack, president of the Don't LA My Burbank PAC, dismissed the outrage in a statement to Fox News Digital, suggesting David's critics were proving the comedian's point about political sensitivity.

"I just hope they’re all okay reading this. They seem to be really emotionally fragile and have a hard time understanding actual humor," Cusack said.

BILL MAHER RECOUNTS LARRY DAVID FALLING OUT, CELEBRITY BACKLASH AFTER TRUMP WHITE HOUSE DINNER

David also mocked progressive approaches to religious tolerance, proposing that White women wear hijabs on weekends in solidarity with Muslim women while Jewish Americans lose the right to refer to themselves as the "Chosen People."

In another proposal, the "Seinfeld" co-creator imagined a socialist society in which comedians who offend audiences would be sent to facilities for sensitivity training. Repeat offenders would face an even more unusual punishment.

"If, however, the re-programming is unsuccessful, the repeat offender will be sent to Pitcairn Island to live with the Bagel People," he wrote.

DAVID MARCUS: WOKE 1.0 IS WHY ENTERTAINERS NEEDED OUR SECRET CONSERVATIVE CLUB

The comedian's mock manifesto drew criticism from self-identified democratic socialists, several of whom questioned his comedic abilities and mocked his age, according to The New York Times.

Zack Wall, a 35-year-old Ohio resident who identified as a democratic socialist but said he was not a DSA member, told the Times that David's essay was disappointing, criticizing the quality of the jokes rather than his decision to target the organization.

"It was just so lowbrow and unfunny. It can’t be the same person who wrote 'Curb,'" Wall said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

David's latest satire comes as democratic socialists gain influence within the Democratic Party, particularly through New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Mamdani has defended the growing socialist movement and candidates who support eliminating Immigration and Customs Enforcement, while declining to explicitly endorse Israel's identity as a Jewish state. The DSA has also publicly supported the boycott, divestment and sanctions movement against Israel and efforts to eliminate U.S. military assistance to the country.

Fox News Digital reached out to David and the DSA for comment, but neither immediately responded.

item.title: Carmelo Anthony says WNBA's next commissioner must prioritize safety: 'Protect the players'
item.description: Carmelo Anthony revealed what his first priority would be as WNBA commissioner, emphasizing player protection and investment in them amid the league's record growth.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA, in its 30th season, continues to set records in terms of viewership, attendance, engagement on digital platforms and more as the league’s growth trends even further upward by the year.

However, despite its popularity, the league faces controversy, including the murkiness surrounding sex reassignment eligibility and national anthem protests.

The good and the bad of the WNBA is what a new league commissioner will be dealing with next season, as NBA commissioner Adam Silver and the WNBA Board of Governors will choose a new one with Cathy Engelbert retiring at the end of the 2026 calendar year.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

He won’t be in the running for the job, but Carmelo Anthony has enjoyed the rise of the "W," and knows what his first order of business would be if he took over as commissioner of the league.

"I’m going to invest in the players," he replied when asked the exact question in a recent interview with OutKick. "You have to invest in the script. If you have no script, there’s no movie, there’s no film. You have to invest in the script, and the script in this case is the players.

"We have to protect the players. We have to protect them all across the board if we really want people to look at this league as the best women’s league in the world. So, you have to be intentional with the players and the script. You have to tighten that and build that, and make them feel comfortable in the situation that they’re in."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Anthony didn’t elaborate on what exactly the players need to be protected from, but he did lead his way into wanting to hear exactly how players feel about anything.

"This is a partnership. It’s not like, ‘You work for me.’ No, we work together to build this. I want to hear everybody. I want to hear the good, the bad, the ugly," Anthony explained. "I want to hear where you guys want to go. I want to hear from the players because if I just come with my business acumen, I have a whole other vision for it.

"It has to be a collaborative situation. And that’s why you see the NBA has grown like that once it became a collaborative season."

The good is over than 91 million unique viewers watching national broadcasts this season, which is more than double the prior season’s reach. There were also a total 3.8 million fans who attended games during the season, with a combined 212 sellouts and averaging attendance rising to 11,474 fans per game – a 21% hike from the previous WNBA high.

The bad and ugly, though, has been a long list in years past, but especially in this season.

Transgender athlete eligibility came a widespread debate after Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham publically opposed biological men competing in women’s sports. It spilled over into Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White, both ex-NBA players, declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft citing the league’s rules.

While the league’s collective bargaining agreement saying, "only players who are women are eligible to play," Engelbert and the rest of the league have not provided a detailed definition of a woman, which is why those like Freedom and White continue to speak out.

CARMELO ANTHONY SAYS LEBRON JAMES AND 76ERS CAN BE 'PROBLEM FOR EVERYONE,' INCLUDING REIGNING-CHAMPION KNICKS

That has spilled into on-court altercations, with Freedom being kicked out of a Chicago Sky-Fever game after Natasha Cloud confronted him at his baseline seat. From broader cultural debates, including race, equity and how the league enforces, there are certainly things the new WNBA commissioner will need to address next season and beyond.

But ultimately, Anthony is loving what he’s seen in terms of the league’s growth, which is what he thinks matters most.

item.title: University of Maryland fires head coach Mike Locksley after five straight losses
item.description: Mike Locksley is out as Maryland football head coach after five straight losses, with Aazaar Abdul-Rahim stepping in as interim for the Terrapins.
item.content:encoded:
The University of Maryland is firing head coach Mike Locksley, sources told OutKick.

The Terrapins have lost five straight games after winning each of their first two of the season over Hampton and UConn, most recently losing to Rutgers at home this past weekend.

Locksley was brought on in an interim basis in 2015 after spending three seasons but was then out of the program until 2019. With the Terps, he was 39-54.

Locksley initially turned the program around, as he went 3-9 in his first full season and then went over .500 in each season from 2021 to 2023. However, since then, the Terps are 10-21.

He will be replaced by defensive coordinator Aazaar Abdul-Rahim, who will be the interim head coach for the remainder of the season, the source added.

Locksley's first head-coaching gig came with New Mexico in 2009, where he spent three seasons and went 2-26. He did not land a head-coaching gig until his interim post four years later.

item.title: Louis Oosthuizen leaves LIV Golf in latest blow to circuit that is seemingly hanging on by a thread
item.description: Louis Oosthuizen cited schedule concerns with LIV 2.0 as a key reason for leaving, with only four players committing before the October 25 deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The next iteration of LIV Golf – whatever that may or may not look like – has suffered yet another blow with former major champion Louis Oosthuizen announcing that he is leaving the circuit.

Oosthuizen, the 2010 Open winner, announced his departure from LIV on social media on Wednesday, while also laying out plans to return to the DP World Tour beginning in 2027.

The South African stated that joining LIV five years ago was "one of the best decisions" of his life, but cited controlling his future schedule on the DP World Tour as playing a key role in him stepping away.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I realised I have a lot more in me, and my biggest fear was that the schedule on LIV 2.0 would be tough to manage," Oosthuizen said on Instagram. "I feel I have a few more years of good, competitive golf left in me, and the only way to be really sharp and competitive is through a schedule I control."

Oosthuizen's announcement comes just days before the Oct. 25 deadline for players to commit to LIV 2.0, and at this point in time, Cameron Tringale, Richard Bland, Ben Campbell, Victor Perez, and Brendan Steele appear to be the only players to have done so.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

While Oosthuizen's departure from LIV doesn't deliver the same-sized blow as Jon Rahm's exit, it is quite the peculiar move.

Oosthuizen is 44 years old and has been with LIV Golf since its inception in 2022, while serving as captain for his all-South African team. Stepping away from LIV, and presumably guaranteed paydays plus an equity stake in the LIV 2.0 model promised to its players, is a noteworthy decision.

You couple those factors with his own note about scheduling issues, and it's hard not to assume that Oosthuizen simply sees the not-so-great writing on the wall regarding LIV's future.

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September after the Saudi Public Investment Fund withdrew all financial support from the league at the end of the 2026 campaign. BC Partners made a financial commitment two days before bankruptcy hearings began in the form of a target of $300 million for an attempted LIV return in 2027.

A lawyer representing LIV Golf reportedly told a federal bankruptcy court judge on October 14 that the circuit will know by the end of the month if it has a future into 2027 or will be shutting down operations.

The DP World Tour recently announced that, unlike in years past, it will not be giving conditional status for LIV players to compete on its tour in 2027, forcing players to choose one route or the other.

item.title: Democrats furious after pollster boosting far-left candidates admits fabricating surveys: ‘Absolute scumbags’
item.description: Wedgewood Polling admitted to fabricating data, shaking key races including the Michigan Senate primary between Abdul El-Sayed and Mallory McMorrow.
item.content:encoded:
Democrats are up in arms after a so-called polling firm that projected far-left candidates as strong contenders in several primaries admitted that it had fabricated its polling data.

Wedgewood Polling, which billed itself as an election survey company, released a statement Tuesday night admitting it used "fabricated numbers" for an "experimental project to demonstrate the vulnerabilities, lack of oversight, and overall low barrier to entry in the modern political polling industry."

The group's polls were cited by Abdul El-Sayed's campaign amid a high-profile primary race against Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow and U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich. The nonpartisan polling aggregator Political Polls also cited Wedgewood in the Wisconsin gubernatorial race, showing socialist Francesca Hong having an edge over Republican candidate Rep. Tom Tiffany, R-Wis.

McMorrow said Wedgewood's numbers led to her donations drying up and reporters having "hounded" her with calls to drop out of the race.

JONATHAN TURLEY: FAKE POLLSTER'S STUNT WAS A RECKLESS GAME WITH REAL RACES

"Sure, a point was proven. Polling is broken. But tens of thousands of people poured their hearts, time, energy, hard-earned money into something they believed in - for a year-and-a-half, and it was treated like a game," she said in a statement on X. "Trust is already at an all-time low. We don't get out of this mess without rebuilding trust. And media - who loves to ride the drama of a pollercoaster - needs to take a hard look at what's legitimate and what's not."

Unlike El-Sayed, who advanced from Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary, Hong lost Wisconsin’s Democratic gubernatorial primary to the establishment-backed candidate. El-Sayed, a former Michigan public health official, is currently locked in a tight race against former U.S. Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich., for Michigan's open Senate seat.

Democrat strategist Jennifer Holdsworth said she ran a super PAC that raised money for McMorrow and that "this poll was used by several donors to pull back funding at a time we were being outspent by $80 million."

MORNING GLORY: THE POLLS GOT MICHIGAN BADLY WRONG. NOW DEMOCRATS MAY FACE A BIGGER RECKONING

Wedgewood's numbers were cited by high-profile outlets like The New York Times and Decision Desk HQ, which both said they have since removed them from their projections.

The Times said it removed 15 polls released by Wedgewood between June and October after it admitted to fabricating data. The outlet said Wedgewood had "answered a series of questions regarding the identities of the pollsters; the methods they were using to draw their sample, contact respondents and weight their polls; and the source of their funding" during its vetting process.

Decision Desk HQ said it removed 17 Wedgewood polls from its projections but that it "has not changed the projected seat totals or chamber control probabilities in the Senate or House."

Wedgewood Polling's statement said it "was never intended to sway an election" but rather was aimed as a "wake-up call" about data integrity and vetting standards.

MYSTERIOUS POLLING FIRM BEHIND FAKE ELECTION SURVEYS CLOSES AFTER ADMITTING ‘SOCIAL EXPERIMENT’

"These people are absolute scumbags," veteran Democratic strategist and former Kamala Harris advisor Mike Nellis told Fox News Digital. "They can try to claim that they have some moral high ground here, but they lied about their polling data, got caught, and are freaking out because they've committed fraud."

"The people responsible for this should be run out of American politics, and if they can be, they should be prosecuted to the full extent of the law," Nellis said. He added that both Democrats and Republicans, as well as the media, should reflect on how polling is verified "because there's likely other people that are doing things like this."

TOP ELECTION SCHEMES ROILING KEY MIDTERM RACES AS BOTH PARTIES ACCUSE RIVALS OF TRICKERY

Independent outlet FiftyPlusOne said it was investigating Wedgewood when it had released its statement. Co-founder G. Elliott Morris wrote on X, "We were investigating Wedgewood for faking their data and emailed them for comment this morning, ahead of publishing the findings tomorrow. They are trying to cover up their fraud with the 'we were doing a social experiment' excuse."

Former Obama staffer Tommy Vietor said on X that Wedgewood's actions amounted to "lying and fraud."

A group called "Wedgewood Polls" had also previously created a GoFundMe to raise money for polling in Nebraska's gubernatorial and Senate races. It raised $500 of its intended $5,000.

"I know they crowdfunded, I believe, a good chunk of their polls," Nellis told Fox News Digital. "Are they going to return that money? And if not, are they going to be prosecuted?"

FOX NEWS POLL: IT’S A LONE STAR SENATE SHOWDOWN BETWEEN TALARICO AND PAXTON

Other Wedgewood surveys showed Democrats with significant edges over Republicans in states like Texas, where a July Wedgewood poll showed James Talarico leading state Attorney General Ken Paxton among Hispanics by 64% to 30%.

Republicans, including President Donald Trump, have long heaped doubt on the veracity of polls.

Polls notably showed former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton with an edge over Trump in 2016 — far from the actual result.

And with the fight for control of Congress coming to a head in November, every data point is being scrutinized as political tea leaves.

Fox News Digital reached out to McMorrow's state Senate office, Stevens' campaign and strategist Lis Smith for further comment.

item.title: Max Factor heir's former lawyer details judge's error that wiped out 124-year rape sentence
item.description: A sentencing error cut Andrew Luster's 124-year prison term to 50 years, and a victim's letter asking for leniency played a key role in the outcome.
item.content:encoded:
A legal error led to Max Factor heir Andrew Luster's 124-year prison sentence being thrown out and replaced with a 50-year term, setting the stage for the convicted serial rapist's release after roughly two decades behind bars, his former attorney told Fox News Digital.

In an interview Tuesday, J. David Nick, who represented Luster during his efforts to overturn the sentence, said the original judge improperly stacked prison terms without making the findings required under California law.

The error led to Luster's original sentence being thrown out in March 2013. He was resentenced to 50 years the following month, while his convictions remained intact.

CONVICTED SERIAL RAPIST ORIGINALLY SENTENCED TO 124 YEARS WALKS FREE AFTER 20, SPARKING OUTRAGE

Court records reviewed by Fox News Digital show that Luster was originally sentenced on Feb. 18, 2003, by Ventura County Superior Court Judge Ken W. Riley.

The sentence included 20 consecutive six-year prison terms for rape convictions, along with a four-year term, totaling 124 years.

Nick explained that California law allows judges to impose consecutive sentences for certain sex offenses but requires specific findings to justify those terms.

Ventura County Superior Court Judge Kathryne Ann Stoltz granted Luster a new sentencing hearing in March 2013 after finding that the original court failed to adequately explain its reasons for imposing consecutive sentences.

HARVEY WEINSTEIN SENTENCED TO 15 YEARS IN PRISON FOR 2006 SEX CRIME IN NEW YORK

Luster, the great-grandson of cosmetics mogul Max Factor, was convicted in January 2003 of 86 felony counts involving the drugging and sexual assault of three women.

At his April 16, 2013, resentencing, Stoltz imposed a combination of consecutive, concurrent and stayed sentences, reducing his prison term to 50 years.

Court records show several rape counts received lower three-year terms rather than the six-year terms imposed during the original sentencing.

JERRY SANDUSKY GRANTED NEW EVIDENTIARY HEARING AFTER ACCUSER RECANTS TESTIMONY

Nick said one of Luster's victims, who had previously been in a relationship with him, submitted a letter asking the judge to show leniency.

The attorney explained that the woman had maintained a long-term relationship with Luster and still believed he had redeeming qualities, despite the crimes committed against her.

Nick paraphrased the woman's message to the judge, saying, "This is really gross what he did, but I think the guy's got some good character and you should be lenient on him."

"She did not approve of what he had done to her," Nick added.

The attorney said the request influenced the judge's decision to impose a lighter sentence on certain counts, estimating that Luster could have received 60 to 65 years in prison without it.

Court records show several defense exhibits were submitted ahead of the resentencing, including one the judge ordered redacted to protect a victim's identity. The docket does not establish whether that exhibit contains the letter Nick described.

Fox News Digital has requested the redacted exhibit and additional sentencing records from Ventura County Superior Court.

CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM

The Ventura County District Attorney's Office, meanwhile, said prosecutors fought to preserve Luster's original sentence and opposed the reduction.

"Our office fought at every opportunity to preserve Andrew Luster's original 124-year prison sentence," the office said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital. "We believed then, as we do now, that drugging women, raping them, and gloating about the crimes on film requires the strongest of sentences."

Prosecutors said they also joined Luster's victims in successfully opposing his early parole in 2024 and 2025.

"However, because of the 2013 resentencing, we knew that this day would ultimately arrive," the DA's office said. "Luster reached his maximum confinement date in October 2026."

The California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation confirmed to Fox News Digital that Luster was released to parole supervision Oct. 11 after completing his legally calculated prison term.

"This is not an early release," CDCR public information officer Kyle Buis said in a statement.

The agency said Luster received 977 days of pre-sentence credit and was eligible to earn additional credits through good conduct, work and participation in prison programs.

CDCR explained that people serving fixed prison sentences can be denied discretionary parole but must still be released once they complete their legally calculated terms, including applicable credits.

Nick also challenged criticism of Proposition 57, a California ballot measure approved by voters in 2016 that expanded parole consideration and prison credits for certain offenders.

He argued that longstanding California sentencing-credit rules already allowed people convicted of certain offenses, including rape by intoxication, to earn credits toward their prison terms.

"He got a couple years off with Prop 57," Nick said, estimating that the measure shortened Luster's time behind bars by about two years.

The Ventura County DA's office also pointed to a 2025 change in California law that now classifies drug-facilitated sexual assaults as violent felonies, requiring offenders to serve a greater portion of their prison sentences.

Prosecutors said the change came too late to affect Luster's sentence.

Although Luster is no longer incarcerated, he must register as a sex offender for life, will remain under parole supervision for three years and is prohibited from contacting his victims, the DA's office said.
